title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 203 (Appointment of key managerial personnel)

content.overview: Section 203 requires every company belonging to such class or classes of companies as may be prescribed to have the following whole-time key managerial personnel: (i) managing director, or chief executive officer or manager and in their absence, a whole-time director; (ii) company secretary; and (iii) chief financial officer. Appointment is by a resolution of the Board containing the terms and conditions of appointment, including remuneration. A whole-time key managerial personnel shall not hold office in more than one company except in its subsidiary company at the same time. A vacancy is filled by the Board within a period of six months from the date of vacancy. Key managerial personnel is defined in section 2(51).
content.glance: Prescribed classes must appoint whole-time KMP: MD/CEO/manager (or WTD in their absence), CS, and CFO; Board resolution with terms; not more than one company (except subsidiary); vacancy filled within 6 months; definition in s. 2(51).
content.study: Every company belonging to such class or classes of companies as may be prescribed shall have the following whole-time key managerial personnel—(i) managing director, or chief executive officer or manager and in their absence, a whole-time director; (ii) company secretary; and (iii) chief financial officer. Every whole-time key managerial personnel of a company shall be appointed by means of a resolution of the Board containing the terms and conditions of the appointment including the remuneration. A whole-time key managerial personnel shall not hold office in more than one company except in its subsidiary company at the same time: provided that nothing in this sub-section shall disentitle such a person from being a director of any company with the permission of the Board. If the office of any whole-time key managerial personnel is vacated, the resulting vacancy shall be filled-up by the Board at a meeting of the Board within a period of six months from the date of such vacancy. Current-law framing: confirm the company is in a prescribed class; ensure MD/CEO/manager (or WTD), CS and CFO are in place as whole-time KMP; appoint by Board resolution with terms; enforce the one-company limit (subsidiary exception); fill vacancy within six months. Definition: s. 2(51).

sections.heading: Mandatory KMP
sections.body: Prescribed classes must have whole-time: (i) MD or CEO or manager, and in their absence a WTD; (ii) company secretary; (iii) chief financial officer.

sections.heading: Board Appointment
sections.body: Appointment by Board resolution containing terms and conditions, including remuneration.

sections.heading: One-Company Limit
sections.body: Whole-time KMP shall not hold office in more than one company at the same time, except in its subsidiary; may still be a director of another company with Board permission.

sections.heading: Vacancy
sections.body: Board fills a vacancy in whole-time KMP office within six months from the date of vacancy.

examples.title: Missing CFO
examples.body: A prescribed-class company has an MD and a company secretary but no chief financial officer. Section 203 requires appointment of a whole-time CFO as well.

examples.title: Dual whole-time office
examples.body: A person is whole-time CFO of Company A and whole-time CFO of an unrelated Company B. Section 203 prohibits holding whole-time KMP office in more than one company at the same time, except in a subsidiary.

hypotheticals.question: Must every private company appoint a company secretary under s. 203?
hypotheticals.analysis: Only companies belonging to the class or classes prescribed for s. 203 must appoint the listed whole-time KMP. Whether a particular private company falls in a prescribed class depends on the rules in force; the section itself does not automatically cover every private company.

distinctions.title: KMP appointment (s. 203) vs MD/WTD/manager appointment (s. 196)
distinctions.left: Mandatory whole-time KMP suite for prescribed classes (MD/CEO/manager or WTD, CS, CFO)
distinctions.right: Eligibility, term and dual-office rules for MD, WTD or manager specifically

misconceptions.trap: Any director can double as company secretary without formal whole-time appointment.
misconceptions.correction: Section 203 requires prescribed classes to have a whole-time company secretary (among other KMP), appointed by Board resolution with terms. Informal dual roles do not satisfy the section.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 203 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Confirm prescribed class. II. Check MD/CEO/manager (or WTD), CS and CFO. III. Test Board resolution and one-company limit. IV. Check vacancy filling within 6 months. V. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Class status; KMP roster; appointment terms; dual-office facts; precise relief.

examTips: One company (subsidiary exception); vacancy in 6 months.

enhancement.definition: Section 203 requires prescribed classes of companies to appoint whole-time key managerial personnel — MD/CEO/manager (or WTD in their absence), company secretary and chief financial officer — by Board resolution, subject to a one-company limit and six-month vacancy filling.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: Prescribed companies must maintain a defined core of whole-time managerial and governance officers so that responsibility is continuously attributable.
enhancement.statutoryFramework: Companies Act, 2013, Section 203; definition in Section 2(51).

Not more than one company (subsidiary exception)
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 203 is the KMP mandate for prescribed classes, complementing the MD/WTD appointment rules in s. 196.
